ambiguities.text: The term 'retroactively activated' suggests these rules were always enforced but the specification notes 'backward compatible' meaning they were never actually violated
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume these constraints represent implicit invariants that were never violated historically, now explicitly codified. Any future violation would cause consensus failure.

ambiguities.text: EIP-7523 (Empty accounts deprecation) behavior differs pre-merge and post-merge but the exact distinction is not detailed
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Refer to EIP-7523 directly for pre/post-merge behavioral differences. Assume post-merge behavior applies to current network state.

implicit_assumptions.description: Historical chain data never violated any of these retroactively activated constraints
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Would require chain reorganization or exception handling for historical violations, potentially breaking consensus

implicit_assumptions.description: No account has ever reached or will reach the 2^64-1 nonce limit through normal operation
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Account would become permanently unable to send transactions, potentially locking funds

implicit_assumptions.description: An attacker cannot forge a transaction signature that appears to come from a contract address
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Could bypass EIP-3607 protection and execute transactions from contract addresses, potentially draining contract funds
